Comment: CloudLab c240g5: as experiment.amazon-300m-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-worst-copy-then-flip-long.json, but with its stream behind the queries: every node runs with --own-reads-first, so an old node serves the stream's reads (RAW_GET) only when its own queries leave room on the device, a few at a time (fusion/read_budget.h). A baseline, the other end of copy-then-flip's trade-off from the stream-first files: the queries keep the 4 nodes' capacity, and the flip waits until the load lets the stream through -- where the load stays above C4, until it ends and the backlog has drained. Everything else, rates included, is that file's; its Comment: CloudLab c240g5, U11's worst case on Amazon 300M, copy-then-flip with the load held to 900 s, lazy-long's window. Under the load its stream moves 95-99 MB/s (105-131 MB/s without; bound by the new nodes' writes), so it flips at about 1700-1800 s, after the load; until then it answers about 880-990 q/s of the 1800 offered, and about 750K queries wait when the load ends. They are answered at about 990 q/s in about 760 s, before the flip, so DrainSeconds 900, where the default 300 would record over half of them as abandoned; the run lasts until the flip either way. Its drain under the load (a flip at about 1700-1800 s with about 1.5M waiting, then about 680 q/s less at C8, keeping up at about 4000-4200 s) needs a longer run and more queries than the 2M file holds. The run sends about 1.57M of them, none repeated. Otherwise experiment.amazon-300m-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-worst-copy-then-flip.json with this reservation's rates: Rate 900 and at 60 s 1800, from C4 1239 and C8 2483 (2026-11-21).
